key_insight: VideoMaMa leverages pretrained video diffusion models as a generative prior to convert coarse segmentation masks into pixel-accurate alpha mattes, achieving strong zero-shot generalization to real-world videos despite training only on synthetic data.
problem_solved: Reduces reliance on scarce, expensive per-frame matting annotations by enabling accurate video matting from coarse segmentation masks and bridging the synthetic-to-real gap.
method: Use a pretrained video diffusion model as a generative prior to refine coarse mask inputs into high-quality alpha mattes.
Train the VideoMaMa model exclusively on synthetic data while designing the pipeline to preserve temporal consistency across frames.
Leverage the model's generative prior to scale to real-world footage (authors build a scalable pseudo-labeling/expansion strategy based on this capability).
impact: Allows practitioners to perform high-quality video matting on real-world content without large-scale manual matte labels, lowering annotation cost and enabling scalable foreground extraction for VFX, AR, and video editing workflows.
